answer: Each epoch, a public randomness beacon picks agents for surprise latency audits. An auditor sends a challenge and expects a signed reply within a tight window measured by its quartz clock. Since one machine can't answer dozens of simultaneous audits in time, every fake identity needs its own hardware and bandwidth. Passing audits earns a non-transferable relic, a history record that raises voting weight slowly, so a sybil farm pays real compute costs for months before gaining influence.
